rationale: Desvenlafaxine (SNRI; t½ ~11h; high discontinuation syndrome risk) to escitalopram (SSRI; t½ ~27h; moderate discontinuation syndrome risk). Switch from SNRI to SSRI — reducing noradrenergic activity, often for blood pressure or sweating. Escitalopram is not a CYP2D6 inhibitor — no interaction with desvenlafaxine during cross-taper. Both are serotonergic — low serotonin syndrome risk at standard doses. Desvenlafaxine must be tapered carefully to avoid discontinuation syndrome. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start escitalopram 10 mg. Continue desvenlafaxine 50 mg. Both drugs present: combined serotonergic load at standard doses is clinically acceptable.
Continue both at same doses. Assess tolerability. If excessive serotonergic symptoms (agitation, tremor, tachycardia) reduce desvenlafaxine earlier.

Stop desvenlafaxine. Continue escitalopram 10 mg. Desvenlafaxine discontinuation syndrome possible at this step — if symptoms emerge, slower taper may be needed. Titrate escitalopram to 20 mg at 4 weeks if response inadequate.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Desvenlafaxine 50 mg → escitalopram 10 mg (standard effective doses). Not pharmacologically equivalent — different mechanisms. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.
